lines.t: I was late for work by a holy mile,
GPS said, “Turn right in a while.”
Came ‘round the bend, what do I see?
A big roundabout laughin’ back at me.
Minivan moms, business ties,
Blinkers flashin’ like fireflies.
I hit the brake, let out a shout,
“Lord, why’d You build this big doughnut route?!”
I’m stuck in the roundabout of patience,
Goin’ in circles, losin’ my concentration.
Everyone’s inchin’, nobody goes,
Blinker on left, but they turn right slow.
Maybe this is how You teach me grace,
In a twelve-car halo at a crawling pace.
If I don’t move, I’ll figure it out—
You’re workin’ on my heart at the roundabout.
Guy in a truck on his phone in lane two,
Hasn’t moved once since half past two.
Little red coupe keeps ridin’ my tail,
Like we’re in the Indy 500 snail.
The light ain’t red, the light ain’t green,
It’s just eternal “yield,” if you know what I mean.
I tap the wheel, start talkin’ to the sky,
“Is this your plan or am I fried?”
Then a whisper cuts through my traffic rage,
“Child, I write your story page by page.
You learn to wait when you can’t get through,
That’s where I do My best work in you.”
I’m stuck in the roundabout of patience,
Goin’ in circles, losin’ my motivation.
Everyone’s honkin’, nobody flows,
Same three cars, twenty-seven laps in a row.
Maybe this is how You teach me grace,
With bumper-to-bumper in a tiny space.
If I don’t move, I’ll figure it out—
You’re slow-cookin’ my will at the roundabout.
Old man in a hatchback waves at me,
Grins and says, “Son, just let it be.
I used to floor it, fuss, and shout,
Now I pray three laps before I get out.”
Lady in the SUV hums a hymn,
Kids throw fries, juice to the brim.
We’re all stuck here, wheels just spin,
But maybe that’s where lessons begin.
[Breakdown – Spoken/half-sung]
“Okay, Lord, I get it, sort of…
When I can’t push through,
You’re saying, ‘Wait, I’m ahead of you.’
So I’ll breathe, I’ll yield, I’ll stay in my lane,
‘Til patience grows bigger than my complaint.”
Still stuck in the roundabout of patience,
But my heart’s got a new orientation.
Same slow circle, different view,
I’m learnin’ to trust that You know what to do.
Maybe every stop and every delay
Is You rerouting me a better way.
So if I’m here ‘til my gas runs out,
I’ll laugh and sing Your name at the roundabout.
One more lap, then I’m finally through,
Wave to the cars like, “Peace be with you.”
Look in the mirror, smile at my face—
Got a little more joy and a lot more grace.
